name: marketplace-ai-visibility-auditor
description: Audits a marketplace or brand website for AI visibility and recommendation readiness: whether assistants can crawl it, read it, attribute it to the right entity, trust its freshness, and whether visitors they send actually find what they were promised. Read-only; emits one evidence-backed report with prioritized fixes.

optional_dependencies: playwright (only for the --render confirmation pass; the audit runs fully without it)
runtime.network: outbound HTTP(S) GET/HEAD to the audited site only

skills.summary: Receives the audit request, builds the shared evidence bundle once, composes every specialist skill, scores the site and emits the single audit report.

Can a machine reach the content at all? robots.txt (including AI-assistant crawler tokens), bot walls and edge refusals, sitemaps, HTTP status and redirect health, canonical and indexability directives, host canonicalisation, important-page discovery, and JavaScript-rendering dependence.

Once reached, can a machine parse the facts? JSON-LD validity and coverage, Product/Offer/Brand/AggregateRating completeness, price, availability, identifiers and attributes, microdata fallback, metadata and Open Graph, semantic HTML, and facts locked in non-text - images or linked documents.

Is the machine-readable version current, self-consistent and corroborated? Date signals, sitemap lastmod honesty, price and availability agreement between markup and visible text, review recency, contradiction detection and declared off-site anchors.

Does the site define who it is unambiguously? Organization and Brand identity, name consistency across title/OG/markup/copyright, product-to-brand relationships, variant modelling, category taxonomy, physical locations as readable entities, stable identifiers and disambiguation signals.

Does a visitor an assistant sends actually land on the answer? Specification depth, comparison attributes, filtering and sorting, reviews, FAQs, shipping/returns/availability visibility, deep-link continuity and orientation affordances.

Can the crawled evidence answer the questions a buyer or shopping assistant would ask? Generates questions from the site's own catalogue and content - never from a stock list - resolves each against the shared evidence bundle, and reports the ones the site cannot answer with the URL it looked at and the snippet it found.

composition.model: entrypoint fans out over specialists, then merges
composition.contract: Each specialist skill exposes analyze(bundle: dict) -> list[Finding] in its scripts/analyze.py. The entrypoint resolves those paths from this manifest, so adding or removing a specialist requires no change to orchestrator code.
composition.shared_evidence: Every URL is fetched at most once by the entrypoint and frozen into the evidence bundle. Specialists perform no network I/O.
guardrails: read-only: GET/HEAD only, no authentication, no site modification
robots.txt honoured for the audited site and for any declared off-site anchor
rate limited, byte capped, time budgeted (< 5 minutes for a typical site)
every finding must cite at least one recorded observation or it is rejected
no third-party services: only the audited site and the anchors it declares are fetched
